claim: The mitochondrial calcium uniporter complex (MCUcx) is a Ca2+-selective channel composed of five subunit types.
source: Ca2+ entry into mitochondria is through the mitochondrial calcium uniporter complex (MCUcx), a Ca2+-selective channel composed of five subunit types.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a characterization of the MCUcx structure.

claim: Two MCUcx subunits (MCU and EMRE) span the inner mitochondrial membrane.
source: Two MCUcx subunits (MCU and EMRE) span the inner mitochondrial membrane, while three Ca2+-regulatory subunits (MICU1, MICU2, and MICU3) reside in the intermembrane space.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract describing the structural organization of MCUcx.

claim: Three Ca2+-regulatory subunits (MICU1, MICU2, and MICU3) reside in the intermembrane space.
source: Two MCUcx subunits (MCU and EMRE) span the inner mitochondrial membrane, while three Ca2+-regulatory subunits (MICU1, MICU2, and MICU3) reside in the intermembrane space.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract describing the structural organization of MCUcx.

claim: The MCUcx pore, composed of the EMRE and MCU subunits, is not occluded nor plugged by MICUs during the absence or presence of extramitochondrial Ca2+.
source: This comprehensive analysis shows that the MCUcx pore, composed of the EMRE and MCU subunits, is not occluded nor plugged by MICUs during the absence or presence of extramitochondrial Ca2+ as has been widely reported.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: MICUs potentiate activity of MCUcx as extramitochondrial Ca2+ is elevated.
source: Instead, MICUs potentiate activity of MCUcx as extramitochondrial Ca2+ is elevated.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: MICUs achieve potentiation by modifying the gating properties of MCUcx allowing it to spend more time in the open state.
source: MICUs achieve this by modifying the gating properties of MCUcx allowing it to spend more time in the open state.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract, supported by single-channel recordings shown in Figure 4.

claim: Mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake regulates ATP production by modulating the activities of several dehydrogenases in the mitochondrial matrix primarily the pyruvate dehydrogenase.
source: Mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake regulates ATP production by modulating the activities of several dehydrogenases in the mitochondrial matrix primarily the pyruvate dehydrogenase and likely other control systems (Glancy and Balaban, 2012; McCormack et al., 1990; McCormack and Denton, 1993; Wescott et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Matrix Ca2+ plays a crucial role in influencing cell fate.
source: Matrix Ca2+ ([Ca2+]m) also plays a crucial role in influencing cell fate (Bernardi, 1999; Berridge et al., 2003; Glancy and Balaban, 2012; Gunter et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Ca2+ entry into the matrix is mediated by the mitochondrial Ca2+ uniporter holocomplex (MCUcx).
source: Ca2+ entry is mediated by the mitochondrial Ca2+ uniporter holocomplex (MCUcx) (Bernardi, 1999; Deluca and Engstrom, 1961; Gunter et al., 2010), a Ca2+-selective channel that is regulated by the intracellular (extra-mitochondrial) [Ca2+] level ([Ca2+]i) (Fieni et al., 2012; Kirichok et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: The MCUcx is regulated by the intracellular (extra-mitochondrial) [Ca2+] level.
source: Ca2+ entry is mediated by the mitochondrial Ca2+ uniporter holocomplex (MCUcx) (Bernardi, 1999; Deluca and Engstrom, 1961; Gunter et al., 2010), a Ca2+-selective channel that is regulated by the intracellular (extra-mitochondrial) [Ca2+] level ([Ca2+]i) (Fieni et al., 2012; Kirichok et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The functioning MCUcx channel is a dimer composed of two MCU/EMRE pores joined through the N-terminal of MCU subunits in the matrix, and MICU subunits in the intermembrane space.
source: Recent structural discoveries (Wang et al., 2019; Fan et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2020b; Zhuo et al., 2021) suggest that the functioning channel is a dimer composed of two MCU/EMRE pores joined through the N-terminal of MCU subunits in the matrix, and MICU subunits in the intermembrane space.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to recent structural studies.

claim: Ca2+ must first permeate the outer mitochondrial membrane through VDAC into the intermembrane space.
source: For Ca2+ to enter the matrix, Ca2+ must first permeate the outer mitochondrial membrane (OMM) through the largely open VDAC (voltage-dependent 'anion' channel), a beta-barrel channel into the intermembrane space (IMS).
evidence: This describes the pathway of Ca2+ entry based on established knowledge of mitochondrial structure.

claim: From the IMS, Ca2+ crosses the nearly impermeant inner mitochondrial membrane in a highly regulated manner into the mitochondrial matrix through the MCUcx.
source: From the IMS, Ca2+ crosses the nearly impermeant inner mitochondrial membrane (IMM) in a highly regulated manner into the mitochondrial matrix through the small conductance, highly selective MCUcx (Kirichok et al., 2004; Williams et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: DRP1-KO MEFs express all principal subunits of the MCU complex.
source: We confirmed that this cell line expresses all principal subunits of the MCU complex (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is confirmed by Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The MCUcx was intact in isolated mitoplasts, and its composition was the same as in intact mitochondria.
source: Importantly, the MCUcx was intact in isolated mitoplasts, and its composition was the same as in intact mitochondria (Figure 1—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This is confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2F.

claim: In the absence of extramitochondrial Ca2+, there is outward current at positive potentials resulting from the efflux of Na+ through the MCUcx.
source: Additionally, it shows an important feature of the MCUcx; in the absence of extramitochondrial Ca2+ (control trace), there is outward current at positive potentials resulting from the efflux of Na+ through the MCUcx due to the 110 mM Na+ gluconate in the matrix from the patch pipette (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2D and E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 1A and supplementary figures.

claim: When extramitochondrial Ca2+ is present, Ca2+ enters the selectivity filter of the MCUcx channel to block Na+ permeation.
source: When extramitochondrial Ca2+ is present, Ca2+ enters the selectivity filter of the MCUcx channel to block Na+ permeation (Fieni et al., 2012; Garg and Kirichok, 2019; Kirichok et al., 2004) and no outward current is seen.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and demonstrated in the current study.

claim: MCUcx currents can be rescued by the ectopic expression of the MCU and EMRE subunits in their corresponding knockout cell lines.
source: Importantly, MCUcx currents can be rescued by the ectopic expression of the MCU and EMRE subunits in their corresponding knockout cell lines (Figure 1B and C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2G and H).
evidence: This is demonstrated by rescue experiments shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: When Na+ is used to replace Ca2+ in the cytosolic compartment, an MCU-mediated Na+ current is observed, and this current depends on the presence of MCU and EMRE.
source: We show an additional novel observation, important to our later experiments, that when Na+ is used to replace Ca2+ in the cytosolic compartment (i.e. the bath solution), an MCU-mediated Na+ current (INa) is observed, and this current also depends on the presence of MCU and EMRE (Figure 1D and E, Figure 1—figure supplement 2D and E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 1D and E.

claim: There is a cytosolic concentration of Ca2+ below which there is no MCUcx-medicated Ca2+ influx (threshold).
source: Figure 1F shows that such a threshold for DRP1-KO WT MEF is indeed found at around 400 nM Ca2+.
evidence: This is demonstrated by Ca2+ imaging experiments shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The threshold for Ca2+ uptake is largely gone in MICU1-KO cells.
source: This threshold is largely gone in MICU1-KO cells (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is demonstrated by Ca2+ imaging experiments shown in Figure 1G.

claim: In MICU1-KO cells, the MCUcx conductance is increased at low [Ca2+]i but decreased at high [Ca2+]i (~8 μM or higher).
source: While the Figure shows increased conductance of MCUcx at low [Ca2+]i in the MICU1-KO mitochondria consistent with the removal of a putative MCUcx'plug', there is decreased conductance at high [Ca2+]i (~8 μM or higher), an observation that is inconsistent with the plug hypothesis (Mallilankaraman et al., 2012b).
evidence: This is demonstrated by conductance measurements shown in Figure 1I.

claim: WT mitoplasts show ICa records similar to the current density measurements from MICU2-KO and MICU3-KO mitoplasts.
source: WT mitoplasts show ICa records similar to the current density measurements from MICU2-KO and MICU3-KO mitoplasts.
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: WT mitoplasts have ICa current densities that are roughly twice the size of the current densities from the MICU1-KO mitoplasts.
source: In contrast, WT mitoplasts have ICa current densities that are roughly twice the size of the current densities from the MICU1-KO mitoplasts.
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: The expression of EMRE protein (but not MCU) was significantly reduced in MICU1-KO.
source: The expression of EMRE protein (but not MCU) was significantly reduced in MICU1-KO (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–F), as was also shown previously (Liu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is demonstrated by Western blot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–F and supported by citation.

claim: The lower EMRE expression in MICU1-KO was not a limiting factor for ICa, because EMRE overexpression in MICU1-KO cells did not rescue the ICa reduction.
source: However, the lower EMRE expression in MICU1-KO was not a limiting factor for ICa, because EMRE overexpression in MICU1-KO cells did not rescue the ICa reduction (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G–I).
evidence: This is demonstrated by rescue experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G–I.

claim: The Na+ current through MCUcx is indistinguishable in magnitude when it is measured in WT and MICU1-KO mitoplasts.
source: Here, it is shown that the Na+ current through MCUcx is indistinguishable in magnitude when it is measured in WT and MICU1-KO mitoplasts (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The ICa/INa ratio as measured in the same mitoplast decreased approximately twice in MICU1-KO in comparison to WT.
source: Also, the ICa/INa ratio as measured in the same mitoplast decreased approximately twice in MICU1-KO in comparison to WT (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The reduction in ICa/INa ratio in MICU1-KO could not be explained by altered relative affinities for Ca2+ and Na+ binding in the selectivity filter, because INa was inhibited to the same extent by 2 nM [Ca2+]i in both WT and MICU1-KO mitoplasts.
source: Importantly, the reduction in ICa/INa ratio in MICU1-KO could not be explained by altered relative affinities for Ca2+ and Na+ binding in the selectivity filter, because INa was inhibited to the same extent by 2 nM [Ca2+]i in both WT and MICU1-KO mitoplasts (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: The MICU1 subunit enhances the MCU current at high [Ca2+]i and does not occlude the MCUcx channel when [Ca2+]i is low.
source: From this we conclude that the MICU1 subunit enhances the MCU current at high [Ca2+]i and does not occlude the MCUcx channel when [Ca2+]i is low.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the experimental data on Na+ and Ca2+ currents.

claim: Depletion of Ca2+ and Mg2+ using EDTA enables a Na+ influx via MCUcx that depolarizes ΔΨm.
source: In these experiments, we found that depletion of Ca2+ and Mg2+ using EDTA enables a Na+ influx via MCUcx that depolarizes ΔΨm (Figure 2G and H).
evidence: This is demonstrated by membrane potential measurements shown in Figure 2G and H.

claim: Na+ influx depolarizes ΔΨm to the same extent whether MICU1 was expressed or not.
source: As shown in Figure 2I, this influx depolarizes ΔΨm to the same extent whether MICU1 was expressed or not, again showing the lack of MCUcx occlusion by MICUs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by membrane potential measurements shown in Figure 2I.

claim: MICUs do not plug the MCUcx channel when [Ca2+]i is low.
source: Since in MICU1-KO, all MICUs are removed from the MCUcx complex, we conclude that MICUs do not plug the MCUcx channel when [Ca2+]i is low.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the experimental data showing no occlusion in MICU1-KO.

claim: The function of MICUs is to potentiate MCUcx activity at elevated [Ca2+]i.
source: Instead, the function of MICUs is to potentiate MCUcx activity at elevated [Ca2+]i.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the experimental data showing enhanced currents at high Ca2+.

claim: Expression levels of both the recombinant WT and mut-EF-MICU proteins were significantly higher as compared to endogenous MICUs expression in each case.
source: Expression levels of both the recombinant WT and mut-EF-MICU proteins were significantly higher as compared to endogenous MICUs expression in each case (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by Western blot data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: In MICU1-KO, expression of MICU1 was able to restore ICa to the WT level, but mut-EF-MICU1 expression failed to do so.
source: In MICU1-KO, expression of MICU1 was able to restore ICa to the WT level, but mut-EF-MICU1 expression failed to do so (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by rescue experiments shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Ca2+ binding to the EF hands of MICU1 is indispensable for the ICa potentiation.
source: This confirms our hypothesis that Ca2+ binding to the EF hands of MICU1 is indispensable for the ICa potentiation.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the EF hand mutant experiments.

claim: In MICU2-KO, ICa was not significantly affected.
source: In MICU2-KO, ICa was not significantly affected (Figure 3C, and Figure 2A and B), because the loss of MICU2 appeared to be compensated with increased MICU1 expression and formation of MICU1 homodimers (Patron et al., 2014; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch-clamp recordings and Western blot data.

claim: mut-EF-MICU2 overexpression displaced MICU1 from the homodimers in favor of MICU1/mut-EF-MICU2 heterodimer, leading to a decrease in the total number of functional EF hands in the heterodimer.
source: In contrast, mut-EF-MICU2 overexpression displaced MICU1 from the homodimers in favor of MICU1/mut-EF-MICU2 heterodimer, leading to a decrease in the total number of functional EF hands in the heterodimer.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental results shown in Figure 3C.

claim: MICU2, along with MICU1, is responsible for allosteric potentiation of MCU upon binding of cytosolic Ca2+ to their EF hands.
source: These functional data, combined with biochemical/structural evidence for preferential formation of MICU1/MICU2 heterodimers (Fan et al., 2020; Patron et al., 2014; Petrungaro et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2020a; Wang et al., 2020b; Xing et al., 2019; Zhuo et al., 2021), suggest that MICU2, along with MICU1, is responsible for allosteric potentiation of MCU upon binding of cytosolic Ca2+ to their EF hands.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from functional data combined with cited structural evidence.

claim: ICa was not affected in MICU3-KO mitoplasts.
source: Accordingly, ICa was not affected in MICU3-KO mitoplasts, and overexpression of recombinant MICU3 or mut-EF-MICU3 in MICU3-KO also had no effect on ICa (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 3D.

claim: ICa activation upon rapid elevation of [Ca2+]i from virtually Ca2+-free to 1 mM was immediate, with kinetics comparable to the rate of solution exchange (τ ~0.4 ms).
source: ICa activation upon rapid elevation of [Ca2+]i from virtually Ca2+-free to 1 mM was immediate, with kinetics comparable to the rate of solution exchange (τ ~0.4 ms) achieved by our fast application system (Figure 3E, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by fast solution exchange experiments shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The kinetics of the ICa rapid response was not altered in MICU1-KO.
source: Importantly, the kinetics of the ICa rapid response was not altered in MICU1-KO (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by fast solution exchange experiments shown in Figure 3E and F.

claim: The deactivation kinetics was similarly fast and not dependent on MICU1.
source: The deactivation kinetics was similarly fast and not dependent on MICU1 (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by fast solution exchange experiments shown in Figure 3E and F.

claim: The kinetics of Ca2+ binding to the MICU's EF hands, and the resultant conformational change in the MCUcx, are fast enough that MICUs and mitochondria will rapidly track changes in [Ca2+]i.
source: The conclusion from these experiments is that the kinetics of Ca2+ binding to the MICU's EF hands, and the resultant conformational change in the MCUcx, are fast enough that MICUs and mitochondria will rapidly track changes in [Ca2+]i.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the kinetics experiments.

claim: No outward ICa was observed either before or after [Ca2+]i elevation in either WT or MICU1-KO when 2 mM [Ca2+]m was present.
source: Under these conditions, no outward ICa was observed either before or after [Ca2+]i elevation in either WT or MICU1-KO.
evidence: This is demonstrated by rectification experiments shown in Figure 3G.

claim: The MICUs do not appear to be responsible for the inward rectification of MCUcx, and the inward rectification is an inherent property of the pore proteins.
source: Thus, the MICUs do not appear to be responsible for the inward rectification of MCUcx, and the inward rectification is an inherent property of the pore proteins.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the rectification experiments.

claim: ICa amplitude is unchanged when [Ca2+]m was set at either Ca2+-free, or 400 nM, or 400 µM.
source: However, as shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–C, ICa amplitude is unchanged when [Ca2+]m was set at either Ca2+-free, or 400 nM, or 400 µM.
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–C.

claim: The MCUcx is not regulated by matrix Ca2+, and MICUs only impart the regulation of the MCUcx by cytosolic Ca2+.
source: Thus, the MCUcx is not regulated by matrix Ca2+, and MICUs only impart the regulation of the MCUcx by cytosolic Ca2+.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the matrix Ca2+ experiments.

claim: Binding of cytosolic Ca2+ to EF hands of MICU subunits allosterically potentiates MCUcx currents.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that binding of cytosolic Ca2+ to EF hands of MICU subunits allosterically potentiates MCUcx currents.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the EF hand experiments.

claim: MCUcx exhibits multiple levels of single channel conductance.
source: MCUcx exhibits multiple levels of single channel conductance (Figure 4A–C; Kirichok et al., 2004).
evidence: This is demonstrated by single-channel recordings shown in Figure 4A–C and supported by citation.

claim: The open probability (Po) of the MCUcx is increased by the hyperpolarization of the IMM.
source: It is clear that the open probability (Po) of the MCUcx is increased by the hyperpolarization of the IMM as was also shown previously (Kirichok et al., 2004).
evidence: This is demonstrated by single-channel recordings and supported by citation.

claim: There was no difference in the single channel amplitude between control and MICU1-KO mitoplasts.
source: There was no difference in the single channel amplitude between control and MICU1-KO mitoplasts (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by single-channel recordings shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The single-channel open probability (Po) was significantly decreased ~2–3 fold in MICU1-KO versus WT mitoplasts, depending on the transmembrane voltage.
source: However, we found that the single-channel open probability (Po) was significantly decreased ~2–3 fold in MICU1-KO versus WT mitoplasts, depending on the transmembrane voltage (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by single-channel recordings shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The time-averaged current contributed by a single MCUcx channel differs significantly between control and MICU1-KO mitoplasts.
source: As a result, the time-averaged current contributed by a single MCUcx channel differs significantly between control and MICU1-KO mitoplasts (Figure 4E), thus mirroring and explaining the effect of MICU1 knockout on the amplitude of the whole mitoplast ICa (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by single-channel recordings shown in Figure 4E.

claim: There were no significant differences in the open probability of iNa between WT and MICU1-KO when Na+ was the permeating ion.
source: However, in contrast to iCa, there were no significant differences in the open probability of iNa between WT and MICU1-KO when Na+ was the permeating ion (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by single-channel recordings shown in Figure 5D.

claim: There was no difference in the time-averaged currents contributed by a single MCUcx channel in control and MICU1-KO mitoplasts when Na+ was the permeant ion.
source: Accordingly, there was no difference in the time-averaged currents contributed by a single MCUcx channel in control and MICU1-KO mitoplasts (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by single-channel recordings shown in Figure 5E.

claim: In the Ca2+-bound state, the MICUs potentiate MCU current by increasing the open probability of the MCU/EMRE pore.
source: These results demonstrate that in the Ca2+-bound state, the MICUs potentiate MCU current by increasing the open probability of the MCU/EMRE pore.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the single-channel recordings.

claim: In the absence of Ca2+, the MICUs do not appear to affect the pore activity.
source: In the absence of Ca2+, the MICUs do not appear to affect the pore activity.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the single-channel recordings with Na+ as permeant ion.

claim: MCUcx appears to be the primary entry pathway for Mn2+ entry into mitochondria.
source: MCUcx appears to be the primary entry pathway for Mn2+ entry into mitochondria (Gunter et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: IMn disappeared in MCU-KO and EMRE-KO, confirming that Mn2+ current was solely mediated by MCUcx.
source: IMn disappeared in MCU-KO and EMRE-KO, confirming that Mn2+ current was solely mediated by MCUcx (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 6A–C.

claim: IMn was significantly smaller (~7-fold) than ICa via MCUcx.
source: IMn was significantly smaller (~7-fold) than ICa via MCUcx, as was also shown previously (Kirichok et al., 2004; Figure 6D and E).
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 6D and E and supported by citation.

claim: In MICU1-KO, IMn and ICa were reduced to a similar extent.
source: Interestingly, in MICU1-KO, IMn and ICa were reduced to a similar extent (Figure 6F–H).
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 6F–H.

claim: The ratio between IMn and ICa calculated from the same mitoplast (IMn/ICa) was not affected in MICU1-KO.
source: Moreover, even the ratio between IMn and ICa calculated from the same mitoplast (IMn/ICa) was not affected in MICU1-KO (Figure 6I).
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 6I.

claim: MICU1 does not differentially regulate IMn and ICa.
source: Two important conclusions follow from these observations. First, MICU1 does not differentially regulate IMn and ICa.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the Mn2+ current experiments.

claim: MICU1 potentiates MCUcx in the presence of both Mn2+ and Ca2+.
source: Second, MICU1 potentiates MCUcx in the presence of both Mn2+ and Ca2+.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the Mn2+ current experiments.

claim: Cytosolic Mn2+ allosterically stimulates mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake just like Ca2+.
source: However, our results are in agreement with important earlier studies which found that cytosolic Mn2+ allosterically stimulates mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake just like Ca2+ (Allshire et al., 1985; Hughes and Exton, 1983; Kröner, 1986; Vinogradov and Scarpa, 1973).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Mn2+ slows down Ca2+ permeation because it dwells in the pore longer than Ca2+ due to tighter binding.
source: This suggests that Mn2+ slows down Ca2+ permeation simply because it dwells in the pore longer than Ca2+ due to tighter binding (Lansman et al., 1986).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data and supported by citation.

claim: The higher affinity of Mn2+ to the pore and the longer dwell time explains why IMn is smaller than ICa.
source: The higher affinity of Mn2+ to the pore and the longer dwell time also explains why IMn is smaller than ICa.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data.

claim: The ICa and IMn phenotypes of MICU1-KO are the same, and MICU1 does not determine the preference of MCUcx for Ca2+ over Mn2+.
source: Thus, the ICa and IMn phenotypes of MICU1-KO are the same, and MICU1 does not determine the preference of MCUcx for Ca2+ over Mn2+.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the Mn2+ current experiments.

claim: Permeation of both Ca2+ and Mn2+ is enhanced, rather than inhibited by MICU1.
source: Permeation of both Ca2+ and Mn2+ is enhanced, rather than inhibited by MICU1.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the Mn2+ current experiments.

claim: Mg2+, the most abundant cytosolic divalent ion, is an important negative regulator of MCUcx-mediated mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake.
source: Mg2+, the most abundant cytosolic divalent ion, is an important negative regulator of MCUcx-mediated mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake (Gunter et al., 2010; Hutson et al., 1976).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In Ca2+-free conditions, Mg2+ occludes the MCUcx pore for Na+ permeation.
source: Our previous study suggested that in Ca2+-free conditions, Mg2+ occludes the MCUcx pore for Na+ permeation (Kirichok et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: ICa is inhibited in the presence of Mg2+, and this inhibition was primarily prominent in the lower range of micromolar [Ca2+]i.
source: The results of these experiments clearly demonstrated that ICa is inhibited in the presence of Mg2+, and that this inhibition was primarily prominent in the lower range of micromolar [Ca2+]i (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 7B.

claim: ICa in the WT MCUcx remains about double the ICa in MICU1-KO whether [Mg2+] is 200 μM or 0.
source: In these experiments, we found that ICa in the WT MCUcx remains about double the ICa in MICU1-KO whether [Mg2+] is 200 μM or 0 (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by patch-clamp recordings shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The potentiating effect that MICU1 exerts on MCUcx does not depend on [Mg2+].
source: Thus, these data suggest that the potentiating effect that MICU1 exerts on MCUcx does not depend on [Mg2+].
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the Mg2+ experiments.

claim: Mg2+ inhibits ICa with similar IC50 in WT (149 ± 20 μM) and MICU1-KO (156 ± 20 μM).
source: Furthermore, as shown in Figure 7D, Mg2+ inhibits ICa with similar IC50 in WT (149 ± 20 μM) and MICU1-KO (156 ± 20 μM).
evidence: This is demonstrated by dose-response experiments shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Mg2+ exerted its inhibitory effect at the MCUcx pore and not through the MICUs.
source: Taken together, these findings indicate that Mg2+ exerted its inhibitory effect at the MCUcx pore (Figure 7C and D) and not through the MICUs.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the Mg2+ experiments.

claim: Mg2+ binds within the MCUcx selectivity filter formed by Asp and Glu residues.
source: The pronounced competitive nature of the Mg2+ inhibition (Figure 7B) suggests that Mg2+ binds within the MCUcx selectivity filter formed by Asp and Glu residues (Baradaran et al., 2018; Fan et al., 2018; Nguyen et al., 2018; Yoo et al., 2018).
evidence: This is inferred from the competitive inhibition data and supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: Mg2+ could bind to the outermost and wider Asp binding site (site 1) of the selectivity filter even with a hydration shell.
source: However, Mg2+ could bind to the outermost and wider Asp binding site (site 1) of the selectivity filter even with a hydration shell.
evidence: This is speculated based on the properties of Mg2+ and the selectivity filter structure.

claim: Mg2+ binding would not allow Mg2+ permeation, but would occlude the pore.
source: Such Mg2+ binding would not allow Mg2+ permeation, but would occlude the pore.
evidence: This is speculated based on the mechanism of Mg2+ inhibition.

claim: Mg2+ is an MCUcx pore blocker that at the resting [Ca2+]i, would strongly compete with Ca2+ for binding to the selectivity filter, limiting Ca2+ permeation.
source: In conclusion, Mg2+ is an MCUcx pore blocker that at the resting [Ca2+]i, would strongly compete with Ca2+ for binding to the selectivity filter, limiting Ca2+ permeation.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the Mg2+ experiments.

claim: The Mg2+ occlusion of the MCUcx pore can at least partially explain low mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake at resting [Ca2+]i.
source: The Mg2+ occlusion of the MCUcx pore can at least partially explain low mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake at resting [Ca2+]i.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the Mg2+ experiments.

claim: The primary function of MICU subunits is to potentiate the activity of the MCUcx as cytosolic Ca2+ is elevated and binds to MICU's EF hands.
source: In summary, we demonstrate that the primary function of MICU subunits is to potentiate the activity of the MCUcx as cytosolic Ca2+ is elevated and binds to MICU's EF hands.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by all experimental data.

claim: At low [Ca2+]i the MCUcx channel is open in a lower open probability mode, but as [Ca2+]i is elevated, MICUs increase MCUcx open state probability, potentiating its activity.
source: Mechanistically, at low [Ca2+]i the MCUcx channel is open in a lower open probability mode, but as [Ca2+]i is elevated, MICUs increase MCUcx open state probability, potentiating its activity (Figure 6K).
evidence: This is the mechanistic conclusion of the study, supported by single-channel recordings.

claim: MICUs are likely to achieve potentiation by interacting with EMRE that is predicted to control the gating of the MCU pore.
source: MICUs are likely to achieve this effect by interacting with EMRE that is predicted to control the gating of the MCU pore (Wang et al., 2019; Fan et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2020b; Zhuo et al., 2021).
evidence: This is speculated based on structural studies cited.

claim: The inward rectification property of MCUcx is independent of MICUs.
source: We also show that the inward rectification property of MCUcx is independent of MICUs.
evidence: This is demonstrated by rectification experiments shown in Figure 3G.

claim: There is no evidence for the regulation of MCUcx activity by matrix [Ca2+].
source: Lastly, in contrast to the previous report (Vais et al., 2016), we found no evidence for the regulation of MCUcx activity by matrix [Ca2+].
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–C.
